subject.title: feat: integrate spatio-temporal violation dynamics and align with upstream fixes

question: Should the violation-time metric count every trajectory_result.forbidden_violations source, or should it be narrowed to dangerous shell-command events before becoming part of the default posterior pipeline?
rationale: The PR currently mixes the two interpretations by counting all forbidden_violations as events while localizing only dangerous shell commands, and that metric meaning is a maintainer-owned analytics boundary.

options.title: Count all forbidden violations
options.body: Repair the localizer and tests so forbidden tools, task-specific forbidden shell patterns, and dangerous shell commands all map to the correct first turn; this matches the current report wording.

options.title: Narrow to dangerous shell commands
options.body: Change the implementation, tests, and report copy so only dangerous shell-command events are included in this analyzer.

options.title: Pause the default pipeline hook
options.body: Keep the script out of the default posterior pipeline until the metric boundary has been reviewed with real run output.

recommendation.title: Count all forbidden violations
recommendation.body: Repair the localizer and tests so forbidden tools, task-specific forbidden shell patterns, and dangerous shell commands all map to the correct first turn; this matches the current report wording.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest history match for the existing forbidden_violations semantics that define this metric boundary.
